headline: High-risk default interaction: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action hazards between Langflow and Open Interpreter.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write uploaded flow files and server-side outputs, while Open Interpreter reads/writes the local filesystem and accepts clipboard/stdin bridges. That creates a plausible default path where Langflow-produced content is treated as instructions by Open Interpreter. The pathway is not fully isolated, but it is broader than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Langflow outputs are copied into Open Interpreter without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, attacker-controlled file content can steer Open Interpreter.
mitigations: Disable clipboard/file handoff between the agents.
Use a read-only export format for Langflow outputs.
Add a provenance header and reject untrusted instructions in Open Interpreter.
Separate the agents into different directories or containers.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored credentials; Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem and broad network egress. In default deployments, data from Langflow can be exposed to Open Interpreter and then transmitted outward through model providers or arbitrary HTTP. The blast radius includes secrets and local files, so this is high.
conditions: IF Langflow stores secrets or sensitive flow inputs in its workspace, Open Interpreter can read them.
IF Open Interpreter forwards those contents to configured model providers or HTTP services, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared files before running either agent.
Run Open Interpreter in a separate user account or container.
Restrict Open Interpreter network egress to approved endpoints.
Store Langflow credentials in an external secret manager.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and broad subprocess/shell execution, and Open Interpreter also modifies git state while Langflow uses server-side shared state. If they operate on the same directory or repo, concurrent writes can corrupt files or commits. The profiles show no locking mechanism, so the conflict is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, write conflicts can corrupt artifacts.
IF Open Interpreter runs git operations in a repo also touched by Langflow, commit/state races can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Avoid letting both agents touch the same git repository.
Pause one agent while the other writes shared artifacts.
Use filesystem snapshots before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents and tools, while Open Interpreter can execute arbitrary code as the invoking user. If Langflow output is fed into Open Interpreter without verification, mistaken or malicious content can become real shell actions or file changes. That makes downstream harm likely and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Langflow-generated text is passed to Open Interpreter as instructions, Open Interpreter may execute it.
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent confirmation bypass, errors cascade into actions.
mitigations: Require human review before passing outputs between agents.
Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter.
Insert a verification step that checks Langflow outputs against source data.
Limit Open Interpreter to non-destructive commands.
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts between orchestration and execution layers.

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets are placed in Langflow and then exposed to Open Interpreter, residency and retention controls can be violated. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Langflow's server-side state and then read by Open Interpreter, retention controls may be bypassed.
IF the local machine contains jurisdiction-scoped data, Open Interpreter can access it beyond intended residency boundaries.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Use separate retention policies for each agent's storage.
Run Open Interpreter on a machine without regulated datasets.
Document data-class handling rules for both tools.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and deletion controls.
